To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the linguistic environment in which learners acquire language is not a random sample of the target language but a modified, simplified, reduced version of it, and (2) that the nature and amount of this modified, simplified, and reduced input, as well as the nature of the interaction that occurs between the interlocutors, have a direct effect on the acquisition of the target language by the learner.
